records.issue_text: Host comparison in website_name logic is case-sensitive: URI(...).host preserves user-typed case while Discourse.current_hostname is lowercase, so URLs like http://Example.com/user on an example.com instance fall through all branches and display just 'Example.com' instead of the full path; fix is to compare website_host.downcase against discourse_host (also affects the suffix check)
records.rationale: In `user_serializer.rb#website_name`, `website_host = URI(website.to_s).host` is compared to `discourse_host = Discourse.current_hostname` using case-sensitive operations (`==`, `split` comparisons, and `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)`). There is no normalization (e.g., `downcase`) on `website_host`, so a mixed-case host like `http://Example.com/user` on an `example.com` instance would fail the `website_host == discourse_host` and suffix/parent-domain checks and fall through to returning just `website_host` (omitting the path).

records.issue_text: Website path is appended without stripping query strings/fragments, so URLs like http://example.com/t?secret=x display with the query string included
records.rationale: The new `website_name` serializer method explicitly appends only the parsed URL path, not the query string or fragment: `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path`. Since it uses `URI(...).path` (and never uses `.query` or `.fragment`), a URL like `http://example.com/t?secret=x` would display as `example.com/t` without `?secret=x`, contradicting the finding.

records.issue_text: Confusingly similar host like forums.example.com.evil.com is displayed as-is when label counts match, though this is not a regression from prior behavior
records.rationale: In `user_serializer.rb#website_name`, the logic for comparing domains is a naive `split('.')` label-count / suffix check (the `elsif (website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length) ...` branch plus the final `ends_with?` check).
